articles.summary: David Perdue, the U.S. ambassador to China, defended President Trump on Friday as the U.S. leader concludes a lavish state visit with Chinese President Xi Jinping without major agreements. “The old adage of deliverables in a relationship that we have with China is really not measurable in many ways,” Perdue said on Fox News’s “America’s…
articles.body:
David Perdue, the U.S. ambassador to China, defended President Trump on Friday as the U.S. leader concludes a lavish state visit with Chinese President Xi Jinping without major agreements.

“The old adage of deliverables in a relationship that we have with China is really not measurable in many ways,” Perdue said on Fox News’s “America’s Newsroom.”

“In some ways, the best thing that we accomplished in this visit is to continue the conversation,” the former Georgia Senator added.

Several Republican lawmakers expressed outward displeasure with Trump’s decision to roll out the red carpet and greet Xi at Joint Base Andrews during the Chinese president’s arrival on Wednesday.

Sen. Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) called on the president in a Wednesday floor speech to “keep in mind” during his discussions with Xi that the Chinese leader is “a brutal, unelected, and oppressive dictator who seeks to dominate his neighbors and whose massive military arsenal is aimed directly at the United States of America.”

When pressed by Fox News’s Bill Hemmer on Friday about whether there were “any breakthroughs” at this summit, Perdue said the leaders established an “AI dialogue” and a “crisis mechanism” for this developing technology.

“I believe that that’s going to be a platform that we can move forward on,” Perdue said.

“This is a very bumpy road we have with China,” he added. “We’re both trying to reach strategic stability, but that doesn’t mean status quo in trade or some of these other political areas. AI is one area that we’re trying to find a way to cooperate.”

Trump has largely brushed aside rising concerns about the potential dangers posed by developing advanced AI technology.

In a Truth Social post on Friday morning, the president called his discussion with Xi a “very productive meeting.”

“Tremendous things will be happening,” Trump wrote. “Like almost everyone else, he seemed to like calling the poorly and inaccurately named Artificial Intelligence to a far more accurate and important name, SUPER INTELLIGENCE. That would be ‘SUPER!’ Everyone last night agreed, also.”

Additionally, Perdue praised Trump for pressing Xi to suspend China’s support for Iran amid the U.S.’s ongoing military operations against the country.

“President Trump did a great job making sure China knows this is unacceptable,” Perdue said. “We’ve seen some movement over the last month as well, but this isn’t the first time President Trump has brought it up with President Xi.”

articles.body:
The five major television networks were back in the White House television pool on Friday following their standoff with the White House over CNN’s access.

CBS broadcast the live feed for television outlets at the White House showing President Trump welcoming Chinese President Xi Jinping back to the White House for the third day of his U.S. state visit, as well as the video feed of the two having tea with first lady Melania Trump and Xi’s wife, Peng Liyuan.

CNN, which was banned by Trump from covering the White House a week ago, also carried the feed.

“CNN’s access to the White House has been restored, and the TV pool appears to be functioning as normal,” CNN anchor Pamela Brown said on air Friday morning .

“As of now, all systems are go,” a person familiar with the pool told The Associated Press .

The development comes after CNN, along with MS NOW and Politico, regained their access to the White House on Thursday. NBC, CBS, ABC and Fox announced earlier this week they were boycotting the television pool over CNN’s exclusion from White House coverage.

On Thursday, a judge ruled in favor of CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, but journalists from the three outlets were initially denied entry into the White House.

The boycott deprived Trump and the state visit of visual major network coverage, though secondary outlets were still in the pool.

Earlier Friday, it was unclear whether the television pool would cover Trump throughout the day. MS NOW and CNN journalists said Thursday their journalists were denied access to the state dinner arrival at the White House, which was a precredentialed event.

articles.title: Let’s fix healthcare costs before the socialists try to do it
articles.summary: Senior fellow Dr. Clifford Porter proposed a series of 11 federal reforms aimed at lowering healthcare costs and increasing patient control.
articles.body:
The reason people are flirting with the idea of socialism is simply that the costs of healthcare and housing are too high and Congress is not solving it. Those in power get the blame. With the seeming internal take-over of the Democratic Party by the Democratic Socialists of America, the promises of quick fixes by punishing the rich corporations are seemingly plausible, with catch phrases like “Medicare-for-All.”

Healthcare is increasingly the No. 1 issue for voters. There is a stranglehold by both hospital and insurance corporate cartels subsidized by government cronyism, profoundly worsened by ObamaCare (the ironically named Affordable Care Act). Voters are now willing to try something else if elected officials won’t act.

Politicians promising “Medicare-for-All,” on the other hand, is a promise they cannot keep. Medicare itself is managed by insurance companies, whose profits are a percentage of premiums, and over-billed by both insurance and hospitals. Eventually, government-run healthcare has to raise taxes or ration medical care. Or, as in the case of Canada and the U.K., they do both.

Healthcare reform was forefront at the Republican Midterm Convention, and there is the opportunity to dramatically improve healthcare through reconciliation before the election or before the new congressional session. The middlemen will lose fortunes with reform, but they are not doing anything to help actual medical care or lower the costs. It is time to bypass them. Current federal rules are causing harm and feeding the cartels. This list of reforms can lower costs 50 percent, by restoring patient and physician control with commonsense reform and a safety net for those who need it.

1. Expand Catastrophic Plans to all ages and incomes. Catastrophic or major medical plans are just that: plans for major high-cost events for which insurance was originally designed. Insurance should not be used for items that are wholesale 90 percent cheaper than insurance rates. The Trump administration has made these recommendations for 2027 with Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services rule changes, but the left is already litigating to block it and keep ObamaCare unchanged. Putting it into reconciliation would make it a law they could not attack and people would have options.

2. Health Savings Accounts for everyone and all plans, including Medicare. HSAs offer individuals the same tax benefits businesses have for healthcare costs. It also gives people lifetime savings for healthcare Medicare does not cover. Cash prices controlled by patients are 50-90 percent cheaper for medications, clinic visits and imaging (x-rays).

3. End ObamaCare-Affordable Care Act restrictions on physicians owning hospitals. This is perhaps the craziest or most cartel-like part of the healthcare law Obama signed in 2010. Research consistently shows physician-owned hospitals are better at providing medical care and better run. Most people are stunned to learn the hospital lobby works hard to prevent competition. Many states, such as North Carolina, allow hospitals to veto competition hospitals from opening.

4. Allow direct primary care clinics to count as primary care for Medicare. It is far better medical care for complex medical cases at a fraction of the price. Hospitals and insurance do not like direct primary care because they do not profit from these clinics or control them. But the purpose of Medicare patients is not to make corporations rich. Also, for patients using Medicare and direct primary care, ban Medicare from blocking medical orders (medications or referrals). This serves only to force patients into monopolistic networks.

5. Clarify IRS rules for direct primary care clinics. Make them HSA-eligible for providing wholesale medications and medical supplies.

6. Expand business options. Let them offer cost-sharing plans and other options outside the Affordable Care Act marketplace with the same tax exemptions (known as ICHRA or CHOICE options).

7. Expand short-term plans. Allow those between jobs or insurance plans to carry short-term plans for up to one year and to renew them for up to three years. Many states have done this —it can be extended nationally by Jan. 1, 2027.

8. Stop Medicare from paying higher reimbursement fees to hospitals than to independent clinics. This has encouraged acquisition of independent clinics and led to healthcare consolidation.

9. End the middlemen’s control over drug prices. Pharmacy Benefit Managers have exemptions from the Anti-Kickback Act. Three of them control 80 percent of the market , and they increasingly control the market with ownership of pharmacies and now manufacturing of pharmaceuticals. Ending these market controls is basic antitrust policy. We should also end their control of access to drugs they deem “speciality” drugs.

10. Fix business insurance. Lastly, business insurance is controlled by Federal ERISA laws. Expanding the concept of “transparency” from prices to all aspects of business contracts, disclosure of conflicts of interest, and kickbacks will restore healthcare markets.

Increasingly patients are held hostage by their own health, and all healthcare professionals are held captive as employees to a few corporations. Administrators determine your medical needs, rather than you and your doctor.

Healthcare reform means middlemen lose business and vast wealth if they lose control over our health. It is like the tobacco industry in the 1980s and 1990s insisting cigarette smoking is not dangerous. Healthcare conglomerates insist they are preventing cost increases even though they are some of the most profitable businesses in the world.

This list of federal reforms is transformational and revolutionary. Reform is easy but the resistance remains staggering. Failure to reform risks frustrated voters reaching for the false promises of the Democratic Socialists of America. Congress has an opportunity to act — just call it the “You Can Have Your Doctor Back Act.”

Dr. Clifford Porter is the Senior Fellow for Healthcare at the Texas Public Policy Foundation.

articles.body:
It’s Friday. We rarely work just 9 to 5 in the media business — but we can still celebrate the late Dolly Parton today with more than one cup of ambition. ☕

Programming note : Hello! We are Colin Meyn and Steff Danielle Thomas filling in for Cate. Please send your tips, comments and story ideas to cmeyn@thehill.com or sthomas@thehill.com .

The White House TV pool was back in action Friday as President Trump and first lady Melania Trump greeted Chinese leader Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan , for morning tea.

Friday was CBS’s turn in the pool rotation, meaning its crew will follow the president’s every move for the day. CNN carried the CBS feed of Xi’s arrival at the White House, a clear signal the standoff with the White House is resolved, at least for now.

Trump on Thursday complained that CNN and MS NOW, which he had banned from the White House, were not covering the “made for Television” state visit. Some reporters for the cable outlets were barred from covering the state dinner Thursday night.

The other four outlets in the TV pool — CBS, ABC, NBC and Fox News — had refused to take their turns this week in solidarity with CNN.

We’ll see how long this lasts: A judge’s injunction ordering the White House to let CNN, MS NOW and Politico back into the White House press corps lasts for two weeks.

As the legal fight continues, it’s unclear if the White House will seek to restrict access for the outlets to certain places, like the Oval Office, as it did for The Associated Press during a similar fight last year.

A key test will come tomorrow when CNN has its next rotation in the TV pool.

Beyond the pomp and fanfare, we’re still waiting on any significant deliverables from the talks between Trump and Xi.

The two gave brief comments to reporters during their tea. Xi said “new substance” was added to the U.S.-China relationship. Trump said many “positive things” happened, adding that American farmers would be “very happy” with the results.

Expectations were low going into the visit. Our friends at the Morning Report had a good rundown of what to watch , while The Hill’s House guru Mike Lillis talked to lawmakers about their biggest priorities — for Insider subscribers only .

🐼 There’s at least one adorable outcome from this visit. Xi announced on Thursday that China would be sending two giant pandas to the Atlanta zoo.

The news comes about two years after Zoo Atlanta sent its previous pandas back home .

📸 The Chinese Foreign Ministry has the deets (and photos) here . Meet incoming ambassadors Ping Ping and Fu Shuang.

Borrowing money is getting more expensive — adding another wrinkle to the affordability debate heading into the midterms.

The latest: The average 30-year mortgage rate climbed above 7 percent this week for the first time since January 2025. At the same time, Treasury yields are reaching levels not seen in decades.

The 30-year Treasury yield briefly hit a 22-year high Thursday, while the 10-year yield — which mortgage rates closely track — is at a 19-year high.

What’s going on?: Investors are navigating stubborn inflation, rising federal debt and elevated energy prices tied to the ongoing Iran war. They’re also bracing for more interest rate hikes after the Federal Reserve raised rates last week.

The effects are already hitting prospective homebuyers. Mortgage rates have risen for five straight weeks and are up from 5.98 percent just before the Middle East conflict began.

That’s unwelcome timing for Republicans, with affordability already weighing heavily on voters ahead of November.

Insiders can learn more from The Hill’s Niall Stanage in his latest Memo.

The Pentagon is scrambling to build support for Trump’s record $1.5 trillion defense budget, but some GOP senators worry officials waited too long to make the case.

The push comes as an additional $87 billion funding request remains stalled — and lawmakers are staring down a narrowing window as the midterms inch closer.

🪖 Insiders can read more from The Hill’s Ellen Mitchell.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has fewer lawyers and a whole lot more work — and newly obtained documents show just how stark the imbalance has become.

Charts obtained by The Hill and NewsNation show staffing across the DOJ’s civil division plunging under the Trump administration while caseloads steadily climb. The department overall has lost roughly 10,000 workers since Trump returned to the Oval Office, according to the data.

Eye-popping numbers : Commercial litigation attorneys are carrying 84 percent more cases per lawyer, while immigration attorneys have seen their workloads jump 63 percent. Appeals attorneys are up 54 percent, while lawyers defending executive orders and other administration priorities are carrying 44 percent more.

The immigration office was also hit particularly hard, shrinking from 320 attorneys to 243 as cases climbed from roughly 7,700 to nearly 9,500 amid the president’s immigration crackdown.

DOJ’s unusual recruiting sweetener: $25,000 signing bonus for new civil division attorneys.

📊 Rebecca Beitsch and Samuel Marks break down the data here .

Federal job cuts are hitting the Washington, D.C., area hard, with 55 percent of residents in a recent survey saying their household has been negatively affected. That rises to two-thirds in the district itself and 62 percent in Virginia’s Arlington and Alexandria.

Another 14 percent of residents across the region said they turned to social services for the first time over the past year.

🏛️ Trump’s plan to turn his proposed triumphal arch into a “top grade military complex” is drawing skepticism from lawmakers and defense experts. The president has floated using the structure to store drones and ammunition, while also placing snipers on its roof and plaza areas.

👩‍⚖️ Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson urged her colleagues to intervene less often in emergency cases, warning the practice carries “institutional costs.” She has repeatedly criticized the high court’s emergency cases.

articles.title: Xi’s 100K invitation to America’s youth sets off alarm bells over what could follow them home
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping's plan to bring 100,000 young Americans to China sparked fears of communist propaganda and potential hostage scenarios.
articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China over the next five years is raising concerns among critics who warn Beijing could use the exchange program to spread propaganda and influence a new generation of Americans. Xi made the announcement Thursday during a White House arrival ceremony, as he visited Washington this week for talks with President Donald Trump on artificial intelligence, intellectual property, trade practices and rare-earth minerals. Xi said China will invite 100,000 young Americans over the next five years for exchanges and study, building on existing programs that have included university visits, summer programs, youth forums and other educational and cultural exchanges. CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE China created its Young Envoys Scholarship program, administered by the China Education Association for International Exchange, to carry out Xi’s earlier 2023 pledge to invite 50,000 young Americans for exchanges and study. Some trips are fully funded, while others require participants to cover expenses, with the stated goal of strengthening ties between Chinese and American youth. While some supported the program, many critics slammed the idea over propaganda and safety concerns. "This is clearly intended to indoctrinate young Americans in China," Manhattan Institute fellow Daniel Di Martino posted to X. "But if some people should go, let the DSA members and let them see the Uyghur concentration camps and poor rural villages. Let them speak to the political prisoners. And let them visit and meet Hong Kongers." "100,000 more Timmy Walz's. What could go wrong," said one user, referencing Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, who taught English and U.S. history in Foshan in 1989 after graduating from Chadron State College. "They’ll come back as Governor of Minnesota," another user added. YOUNG AMERICANS BREAK SHARPLY FROM OLDER AMERICANS ON CHINA THREAT, NEW POLL FINDS "No! They will brainwash them while over there," said one person. "I welcome Xi Jinping’s invitation for 100,000 American students to visit and study in China. As Co-Chair of the Congressional International Exchanges Caucus, I believe educational and cultural exchanges are an important way to build mutual understanding and expertise," said Democratic California Rep. Ami Bera. "But those exchanges depend on trust and the ability to study, speak, and engage without fear of harassment or arbitrary detention," Bera continued. "Right now, American scholar Min Zin remains wrongfully detained in China, and Beijing continues to target scholars, human rights advocates, and diaspora communities whose work or speech it finds unwelcome." "I’m one of the Americans who spent years living and studying in China. I majored in Chinese literature in college. Sadly, I cannot recommend young Americans do the same thing today," said Atlantic Council visiting fellow Isaac Stone Fish. US WARNS AMERICANS ABOUT EXIT BANS AND 'UNJUST' DETENTION IN POPULAR DESTINATION Fish said that China has grown more repressive and less welcoming to foreigners. "If tensions worsen between the United States and China, those students could effectively function as hostages," Fish added. "Are they coming back as Communists," asked one user. "To be honest, I'm not sure I WANT 100,000 impressionable American students sent off to some CCP-controlled propaganda tour," said conservative commentator Nick Sortor. TRUMP TO ASK XI TO FREE WRONGFULLY DETAINED US CITIZEN AS WIFE SPEAKS OUT The Department of Education referred Fox News Digital to the White House when asked for comment. Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment. U.S. authorities have separately warned that American students abroad can become targets for foreign intelligence recruitment, citing past cases involving China. Glenn Duffie Shriver, a Michigan student who studied abroad in Shanghai in 2002–2003, returned to China after graduating in 2004 and was recruited there by Chinese intelligence officers. Shriver was paid to apply for positions with the State Department and CIA to access classified information for the Chinese. articles.body:
Ed Sheeran has canceled his concerts at Gillette Stadium near Boston this weekend because of an incoming nor’easter storm.

The canceled shows follow controversy after the artist Macklemore was dropped from the bill following his comments supporting the pro-Palestinian movement at a concert this month.

Tour promoter Messina Touring said in an Instagram post that the shows scheduled for Friday and Saturday nights were canceled because of severe weather with safety in mind.

“Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium,” Messina Touring said. “The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority.”

The area is under a wind advisory until Sunday morning and is expecting potential gusts up to 50 miles per hour. The tour promoter said refunds are available for all ticket holders.

Severe weather is expected across the New England area with officials preparing for power outages, flight cancellations and other disruptions. Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey (D) said heavy rain and winds are expected and encouraged residents to take caution.

“We’re keeping a close eye on the forecast and coordinating with local and federal public safety partners. Be ready for possible flooding and power outages,” Healey said in a statement.

Sheeran has taken heat from fans after Macklemore’s ouster from the tour.

At least four other opening acts pulled out in protest and support for the artist. Sheeran lost nearly half a million Instagram followers . Sheeran apologized to fans at one show and said the debate has cost him close, personal relationships.

Robert Kraft, owner of Gillette Stadium and the New England Patriots, originally barred Macklemore from performing at his stadium and allegedly pushed other stadiums to do the same, spurring his removal from the tour.

Kraft said the stadium has a commitment to providing a welcoming environment for guests and that Macklemore’s statements, which Kraft deemed antisemitic, crossed a line. He said the artist has a history of antisemitic imagery.

“Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line,” Kraft said in a statement.

Macklemore refuted Kraft’s claims of antisemitism and defended his comments as criticism of Israel, not hate against Jews.

“When criticizing Israel, opposing Zionism or saying ‘Free Palestine’ gets conflated with hatred of Jewish people, it doesn’t protect Jewish people. It protects Israel from accountability,” he said.

articles.title: Senior White House spokesperson to move to Office of Director of National Intelligence
articles.summary: White House senior deputy press secretary Kush Desai is leaving the West Wing for a senior communications role at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI). The White House spokesperson will become assistant director of national intelligence for strategic communications and is leaving next month, Desai told NewsNation. He is helping search for…
articles.body:
White House senior deputy press secretary Kush Desai is leaving the West Wing for a senior communications role at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI).

The White House spokesperson will become assistant director of national intelligence for strategic communications and is leaving next month, Desai told NewsNation. He is helping search for his replacement at the White House as he prepares to make the move, according to Axios.

He had reportedly been discussing a move to the ODNI since new Director Jay Clayton’s confirmation in early August, who took over the agency following former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard’s resignation.

Desai has been a key spokesperson on economic and domestic policy in the administration, fielding questions on tariffs, inflation, prescription drug prices and the Federal Reserve.

He joined the White House at the start of President Trump’s second term as a deputy press secretary after working for the Republican National Committee (RNC) and Trump’s 2024 campaign.

Desai had served as the RNC’s deputy battleground states and Pennsylvania communications director, as well as communications director for Iowa’s Republican Party.

He later rose to senior deputy press secretary and special assistant to the president.

Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt praised Desai, calling him “one of the smartest and hardest working people I’ve met in Washington,” according to Axios.

The move comes less than two months after Clayton took over as director of national intelligence following Gabbard’s tumultuous tenure.

The new position puts Desai in charge of strategic communications at the agency responsible for coordinating the nation’s intelligence community.

articles.title: Reporter's Notebook: Democrats face an impeachment tractor beam that could derail their affordability message
articles.summary: Like the Millenium Falcon caught in a tractor beam, Hakeem Jeffries and House Democrats face an impeachment pull they may not be able to escape.
articles.body: In the original Star Wars, Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, Chewbacca and Obi-Wan Kenobi find the Millennium Falcon under fire from Imperial TIE fighters in deep outer space. Luke speculates that the TIE fighters are "heading for that small moon." But Obi-Wan’s visage grows grim. "That’s no moon," intones Obi-Wan. "It’s a space station." Han Solo disagrees. "It’s too big to be a space station," says Han. To which, Obi-Wan instructs him, "Turn the ship around." But as quickly as he dismissed Kenobi’s observation, Solo pivots. He grimaces, realizing that the wise Jedi Knight is on to something. DEMOCRAT AL GREEN TO FORCE HOUSE-WIDE VOTE ON IMPEACHING TRUMP "Yeah. I think you’re right," Han replies. The Millennium Falcon starts to shake. "Chewie, lock in the auxiliary power," Han commands his shipmate. "Why are we still moving towards it?" squeaks Luke. "We’re caught in a tractor beam and it’s pulling us in!" shouts Han. And a few moments later, the Millenium Falcon, the fastest ship in the galaxy, is suctioned into Bay 327 of the Death Star, moored, and unable to escape. The band of ragtag heroes are now stuck. On the Death Star. Grand Moff Tarkin describes it as "the ultimate power in the universe." +++++++ Impeachment in Congress is kind of like the Death Star’s tractor beam. You can’t escape once you’re in its clenches. A decision to impeach sucks a political party in, eventually marooning everyone in the political equivalent of a hangar bay. For Democrats, they can’t focus on the price of eggs and milk. There’s little debate about gas prices. It’s a challenge to even address oversight issues. You can try to "lock in the auxiliary power." But it’s too late. You might think impeachment is "a moon." But it’s really the political Death Star. Not for your adversary. But often those orchestrating the impeachment. Democrats might find themselves in an impeachment bind if they capture the majority next year. Progressives and the left will possess one of the loudest voices in Congress. And even though Democrats twice impeached President Trump in 2019 and 2021, some will insist on doing it again. That’s to say nothing of trying to impeach a host of Trump Administration cabinet officials – ranging from Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Some Democrats are already falling prey to the impeachment tractor beam. Rep. Al Green, D-Texas, led the initial effort to impeach President Trump during his first term in 2017 – long before the successful impeachment over Ukraine in 2019. Republican redistricting – engineered by President Trump forced Green out of his Houston-based district earlier this year. But Green engineered yet another effort to impeach the President last week as the Texas Democrat heads for the exit. MIDTERM HISTORY MASSIVELY FAVORS DEMOCRATS. BUT THEY ARE MAKING A BIG MISTAKE The House voted to sidestep Green’s impeachment resolution, 232-147. So this was not a straight, up or down vote on impeachment. It was one step removed. Forty-seven Democrats voted "present." That includes the party’s top three Democrats: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., House Minority Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA) and House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif. In some respects, House Democratic leaders want to shun impeachment. Or at least avoid it for the time being. In 2006, Democrats were on the precipice of flipping control of the House. Democrats largely won the midterms that year because of voter fatigue with President George W. Bush and the calcification of the war in Iraq. Many Democrats wanted to impeach the President. But as she prepared to clasp the gavel, then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., famously declared that impeachment was "off the table." House Democrats focused on drawing down the war in Iraq and eventually pivoting to other policy issues like health care and climate change. But Democrats had to get through those midterms first. So once Pelosi said no impeachment, there was no impeachment of the President. Impeachment with President Trump was kind of "off the table" for Pelosi when Democrats reclaimed the House in the 2018 midterms. But there was a shift among moderate Democrats after disclosures about the President and Ukraine in the summer of 2019. A master of the political pulse, the Speaker understood the direction this was going among her Members. That’s when Pelosi got in front of her caucus, pushing for potential impeachment of the President later that year. House Democratic leaders are depositing any overt discussion of impeachment on the backburner for now. They don’t want to veer away from their message about affordability. In fact they’ve frequently steered the conversation back to the cost of living when pressed about impeachment. Consider this response from Jeffries when questioned about impeachment on April 9. "We'll have a conversation led by (Rep.) Jamie Raskin, D-Md., the top Democrat on the Judiciary Committee, and (Rep.) Jerry Nadler, D-N.Y., a former Judiciary Committee Chairman and Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y., and Judiciary Committee Democrats tomorrow about Trump administration accountability," replied Jeffries. But, unlike completely mimicking Pelosi’s posture years ago, Jeffries signaled he was open to the impeachment question. "I don't want to get out ahead of that discussion. But we've also been very clear. House Democrats are going to focus on making life more affordable for the American people," said Jeffries. On June 14, Kristen Welker of NBC asked Jeffries if his party could "move to impeach President Trump" if Democrats reclaimed the House. "We haven't ruled anything in or ruled anything out in terms of accountability. What we have said is that our focus is going to be to make life more affordable for the American people," answered Jeffries. On August 25 on CNN, Jeffries deflected a similar impeachment inquiry. "We haven't ruled anything in and we haven t ruled anything out," stated Jeffries. Impeachment interrogatives continued for Jeffries during a September 13 interview on ABC. "We haven't ruled anything in and we haven't ruled anything out in terms of impeachment," said Jeffries. That’s smart politics for Jeffries. He’s trying to keep his hand on the helm before the midterms – and essentially deferring to the political climate of next year and where rank-and-file Democrats might fall next year should Democrats capture the majority. But there are indications that many Democrats are already ready for impeachment. The progressive base will demand action. And it extends well beyond Al Green. Rep. Madeleine Dean, D-Pa., made her case after the President posted to social media in April that "a whole civilization will die tonight" in reference to Iran. "If that's not high crimes and misdemeanors - and if it's not madness - I don't know what is," said Dean. Rep. Sara Jacobs, D-Calif., said that the President was "threatening genocide." Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said the party should "push for impeachment" and that the President "is unfit to be the Commander in Chief" and "should be removed." So Jeffries has a decision to make. The hard left will demand impeachment – for someone. Be it the President or Hegseth. But if Democrats flip the House, their "majority makers" might represent battleground districts. Those prospective lawmakers will be moderates. Impeachment could be politically toxic for them. TRUMP COULD FACE IMPEACHMENT IF DEMOCRATS SEIZE HOUSE MAJORITY, GOP LEADER WARNS Pelosi’s circumstances evolved in the summer of 2019. Moderate Democrats with national security credentials from swing districts edged toward impeachment. So, she pulled the impeachment trigger. Pelosi knew the direction of her caucus. In September 2026, it’s not as clear for Jeffries. And it’s not a done deal that Democrats will seize the majority. That’s why the New York Democrat expressed caution during his conversation on ABC. "We've got to follow the facts. Apply the law. Be guided by the Constitution and then let the chips fall where they may, in the best interest of the American people," said Jeffries. +++ Han Solo was skeptical back on the Death Star. "Even if I could take off, I’d never get past the tractor beam," said Solo. "Leave that to me," promised Obi-Wan Kenobi. The Jedi Master then eluded detection on the Death Star, manually shutting off the tractor beam. That disgorged the Millenium Falcon. But in the end, Kenobi sacrificed himself for the mission. On Capitol Hill, impeachment is a tractor beam. Once you’re siphoned in, nothing can escape its grasp. Debates about policy. Spending. Health care. War. The tractor beam controls all. Until it’s switched off. Not every party which is incapacitated by impeachment has an Obi-Wan Kenobi who can find the off switch. When it comes to impeachment best advice might be to "turn the ship around" beforehand. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But if lots of Members are clamoring for impeachment, it may already be too late.

articles.title: Lesbian bars are dwindling across the US. How online outrage over mask policy dispute thrust one into the spotlight
articles.summary: The bar had required masks for six years before the owner eased the rule.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Lesbian bars have been disappearing across the country for decades.

With only 36 lesbian bars left in the entire country, according to the Lesbian Bar Project , one of the last ones standing getting caught in a fight over its own mask policy raises a bigger question: Why fight over rules for a bar that might not be around much longer anyway?

That’s the argument Jane Velez-Mitchell, founder and host of the nonprofit streaming network UnchainedTV, made on NewsNation’s “Katie Pavlich Tonight,” discussing backlash against Last Ditch in Greenfield, Mass., after its owner proposed easing a mask mandate in place since 2020.

The number of lesbian bars across the U.S. has been shrinking since the 1980s, when they numbered around 200, according to Newsweek .

“We deal with misogyny and violence and threats that make us want to maintain some exclusivity with who is welcomed into the spaces,” the former general manager of New York City’s Cubbyhole told the outlet. “It’s really important that lesbian bars hold space for everyone’s gender journey.”

Amid changing dietary habits and the rise of app-based dating, some say bars just aren’t an attractive venue anymore.

“We don’t need to go to bars to meet people anymore,” Velez-Mitchell said. “That’s why lesbian bars are closing.” She pointed to online dating and said some patrons are also drinking less, describing herself as a “sober lesbian vegan” who doesn’t rely on bars to socialize.

Beck & Stone senior consultant Emma Jo Morris acknowledged some business logic in catering to existing customers, saying “you don’t tell your client what your client wants… your job is to serve the client.”

Host Katie Pavlich pushed back, saying she believed “the general public is over” masks and said keeping the rule could cost the bar new business.

After making national headlines, the bar has been flooded with critical online “reviews” from people thousands of miles away.

Velez-Mitchell said the shrinking market predates this controversy, however. Last Ditch got its name, she said, because two other gay bars in the area had already closed. She tied the decline to changing times rather than any single policy, pointing to how routine public visibility has become for gay couples.

“I just walked for an hour with two friends of mine, a lesbian couple. They were holding hands the whole way and nobody blinked,” she said, adding that the same walk would have drawn stares 22 years ago.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror ready to return to normal: Reports
articles.summary: Jurors have been in the spotlight after the divisive case ended in a mistrial.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — The holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy case is ready to get back to normal after a surge of publicity following the trial.

Michael Desronvil said he is planning to return to his day job next week, with his attorney Edward Patlzik telling TMZ that his client had been laying low since the end of the trial .

The trial for Lindsay Clancy, accused of killing her three young children, lasted more than five weeks, followed by seven days of jury deliberations. The case ended in a mistrial after jurors were unable to reach an agreement.

Desronvil needed time to process what happened, Paltzik said, spending time with his girlfriend and attending church.

He made headlines after being revealed as the lone juror voting to find Clancy guilty.

Prosecutors argued that Clancy had committed a premeditated crime when killing her children, while the defense argued that she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and not criminally responsible for her actions.

The jury of nine women and three men was split, with 11 jurors voting to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity.

Following the trial, the jury foreperson and other jurors came forward with criticisms of Desronvil, suggesting that he was ignoring the judge’s instructions on reasonable doubt.

He denied those allegations , saying he believes Clancy is guilty of the crime.

Since the trial, he said he had been doxxed and had his personal and legal history made public by people online who disagreed with his position.

Defense Attorney Kevin Reddington has called for an investigation into Desronvil to examine his conduct during the trial, his answers on a pretrial questionnaire and allegations that he used his cell phone during deliberations.

Paltzik pushed back against that motion , saying that investigating jury members would have a chilling effect on people’s willingness to serve on a jury and start a cycle where lawyers investigate any jury when they disagree with the results.

articles.body:
President Trump criticized former President Barack Obama for hosting Chinese presidents for state dinners, including Xi Jinping, multiple times over a decade before doing it himself.

Trump personally greeted Xi at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday and hosted a state dinner for him on Thursday.

But back in 2016, Trump criticized state dinners, saying, “we shouldn’t have dinners at all.”

“We should be eating a hamburger on a conference table, and we should make better deals with China and others and forget the state dinners,” he said at a rally, adding that they “cost a fortune.”

In 2015, he said on Fox News that he wouldn’t be throwing Xi a state dinner.

“I would not be throwing him a dinner…I’d get him a McDonald’s hamburger and I’d say, ‘We gotta get down to work,’” he said at the time . “You know, we’ll give him a state dinner and what he’s done is sucked all of our jobs and he’s sucked the money right out of our country.”

He slammed Obama in 2012 for hosting then-Vice President Xi, including his visit to the Pentagon where he received military honors.

“So wrong! @BarackObama is hosting China’s VP Xi Jinping today at the Pentagon with a full honor ceremony with music and cannons…” he wrote.

He also criticized Obama in 2011 for hosting then-Chinese President Hu Jintao for a state dinner.

“We have the president of China come a few months ago to Washington and we give him a state dinner,” he said at the time . “Now, when people are screwing you, you don’t give them state dinners.”

The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment.

Trump rolled out the red carpet for Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on the tarmac of JBA. They were greeted by military bands, two children bearing bouquets, a canon salute and a flyover of two B1 bombers.

Xi was in the U.S. for a three-day state visit. But his visit received criticism from lawmakers on both sides of the aisle.

“I know the President intends to discuss trade and AI with the Chinese leadership — and rightfully so… But, during every minute of dialogue, our commander-in-chief should keep in mind that his guest is a brutal, unelected, and oppressive dictator who seeks to dominate his neighbors and whose military arsenal is aimed directly at the United States of America,” Sen Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, said on the Senate floor Tuesday night.

A group of Democratic senators released a statement slamming Trump’s invite to Xi.

“As Americans face rising prices for gas, food, housing, and more, President Trump is rolling out the red carpet for President Xi and hosting closed-door dinners so his billionaire friends can strike deals that threaten American jobs and national security,” they wrote.

When Trump traveled to Beijing earlier this year, he also got a red carpet at the airport but was greeted by China’s Vice President Han Zheng instead.

Trump praised Xi’s visit Friday, saying “tremendous strides” have been made for both countries.

“A lot of very positive things happened, but America is very happy about this visit, and I’m sure China is very happy also,” he continued. “Great things for both countries, and it’s been just very, very productive.”

articles.title: James Comey seashells case delayed until early 2027
articles.summary: The seashells-based prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey has been delayed until early 2027, as a judge makes her way through a number of pending motions, including a request by Comey to dismiss the case on grounds it was driven by Donald Trump’s animus.
articles.body: The seashells-based prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey has been delayed until early 2027, as a judge makes her way through a number of pending motions, including a request by Comey to dismiss the case on grounds it was driven by Donald Trump’s animus. U.S. District Judge Louise Flanagan declined to set a trial date in the case against Comey, where prosecutors say that photo he posted on Instagram of seashells in arranged to spell out “8647” amounted to a threat against the President. The term “86” is widely considered to be restaurant slang for running out of or cancelling an item, and 47 is thought to be a reference to the 47th president. Comey, who has not entered a plea yet in the case, had been set to be arraigned on Wednesday at a federal courthouse in New Bern, North Carolina, but Flanagan pushed the arraignment until January. Comey’s team had asked to delay the case. “The gravity of the charges, pending motions, and the need to provide defense counsel additional time to prepare for trial promote need for continuance,” Flanagan wrote in an order Friday. Comey’s extensive legal team has filed numerous motions to dismiss the case, which has come under intense scrutiny from legal experts. Comey’s team contended the prosecution was “not based on a good-faith application of the law to the facts; instead, it effectuates a yearslong campaign by the President to use the criminal process to punish Mr. Comey for his protected speech and because of the President’s deep-seated animosity.” Comey’s team also spotlighted what they call the “extreme bias” of a key witness in the seashells case: an estranged associate of the Comeys who said they hoped Comey went to jail. The lead prosecutor in the case, a rookie federal prosecutor named Matthew Petracca, left the prosecution in May.
